analyzed_vuln.description: Heap-use-after-free due to double destruction of the same closure zval held in executor globals. The PoV installs a user error handler closure and then triggers execution that frees that closure object earlier (via array destruction path), but the stale reference remains in EG(user_error_handler). During request shutdown, zend_shutdown_executor_values() unconditionally calls zval_ptr_dtor(&EG(user_error_handler)), which decrements/frees already-freed refcounted memory (crash observed in zend_gc_delref).
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Input script sets a closure as error handler (`set_error_handler(function(){...})`) and performs `[]=$a[$\xff]=''`-style assignment that causes complex temporary destruction (ZEND_ASSIGN_DIM... handler) and early object free through rc_dtor_func/zend_objects_store_del. The closure object allocated in zend_closure_new is freed during execution, but EG(user_error_handler) is not invalidated before shutdown. On php_request_shutdown -> zend_shutdown_executor_values, destructor runs again on dangling pointer, causing UAF.
